inflation_management: New Caledonia is a French collectivity using the CFP franc pegged to the euro; monetary policy comes from Paris and there is no IMF data series. Inflation tracks euro-area conditions plus the territory's high cost structure. The nickel industry - the economic core - drives activity cycles more than prices: when nickel boomed, construction and services ran hot; the post-2022 nickel price collapse cooled the economy sharply.
debt_management: Public finances depend on French transfers and nickel revenues, a fragile mix: the 2023-24 nickel crisis (high costs, Indonesian competition) pushed major producers toward closure and blew out the fiscal outlook, requiring French emergency support. The territory cannot borrow as a sovereign; Paris is the lender and backstop of last resort. Each nickel downturn becomes a political crisis because the industry is also the independence debate's economic stake.

key_events.event: Three independence referendums (2018, 2020, 2021) all rejected independence, the last boycotted by separatists.
May: riots over electoral-roll changes killed over a dozen people and caused massive damage in Noumea.
Nickel industry crisis deepened as producers sought buyers or closure amid price collapse.

outlook_next_decade: New Caledonia is the Pacific's most politically fragile economy: the 2024 riots showed the independence question is unresolved and the nickel model is broken at current prices. France will keep funding stability, but the institutional future (a new autonomy statute was under negotiation) is uncertain. The base case is French-supported stagnation with periodic unrest; any durable settlement requires both a political deal and a viable nickel future.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
